llm.summary: The skill’s Softr connector purpose is coherent, but its setup instructions include unverified remote installer commands that can execute arbitrary code.

dimensions.detail: Normal Softr operations through oo are proportionate, but the installer commands would run with the invoking user’s local privileges and are broader than needed for a narrowly scoped Softr connector skill.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill documents curl-to-bash and PowerShell irm-to-iex installers from cli.oomol.com; these are mutable remote scripts executed directly without pinning, checksum, signature verification, or review.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime use is scoped to Bash(oo *) and the safety section requires confirmation before write or destructive actions, but first-time setup tells the agent to run setup steps after failures without requiring explicit approval for installer execution.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact itself contains no bundled executable, persistence mechanism, local credential harvesting, or hidden background behavior; any persistence risk comes from the external installer that is not included for review.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill is clearly for Softr CRUD operations through the OOMOL oo CLI, with read/write/destructive actions labeled and credentials described as injected server-side rather than handled by the agent.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. The Softr actions are clearly described and write/delete operations require confirmation, but do not run the documented curl-to-bash or PowerShell iex installer unless you trust OOMOL’s installer endpoint and are comfortable executing unreviewed remote code. Prefer a verified, versioned installer or official package-manager flow if available.
llm.findings:
[PE3] expected: The cited text only says Softr databases are accessible to the connected Personal Access Token; the skill states OOMOL injects credentials server-side and does not instruct reading local token files, so this does not substantiate credential theft.
[SC2] unexpected: The first-time setup section really does include direct remote-script execution for installing the oo CLI; installing a CLI is purpose-adjacent, but this unsafe unverified mechanism is a material review concern.
[T03] unexpected: The static finding is supported by artifact lines 66 and 70, which pipe remote installer responses directly into Bash or PowerShell; this creates a mutable code-execution path outside the reviewed artifact.
